input.body:
Job Id: NBL-008-3466
Address: Flat 5, 55 Lantern Quay, Cedarford, ZZ2 4ZZ

Hello,
Thank you for your estimate of £1,370.00 for the check-out works. We have sent it to the landlord for approval – please do not start any works or invoice until we confirm an order.

To finalise, please could you reply with:
1. An itemised breakdown per item (bathroom sand/fill/damp paint; main room walls and ceiling; bathroom lino; plug; shelf; bath tap), and confirm whether the price includes VAT.
2. "Repair plug socket" – the check-out report records a broken BASIN PLUG in the bathroom, not an electrical socket. Please confirm which you mean. Any electrical socket work would need a NICEIC/NAPIT-registered electrician.
3. Bath tap – we asked for the dripping bath tap to be repaired. Please confirm whether a repair (washer/cartridge) is possible or why a full replacement is needed, with the price of each.
4. The report notes water egress from the shower area damaging the boxing and flooring. Please confirm the cause (e.g. sealant, tray, waste) and whether resealing/repair is included, so the new lino and paint are not damaged again.
5. Bedroom carpet – noted that you consider replacement unnecessary; please confirm whether you can quote for a professional clean of the stains, or advise if this is outside your trade.

Regards,
Northbridge Lettings

Address: Flat 5, 55 Lantern Quay, Cedarford, ZZ2 4ZZ

Hi,
Please find attached a quote for this property. Can you please advise if you approve for me to raise an order for these works.

Quote: Alder Compliance, dated 03/04/2025 – £1,370.00 (VAT not stated). Scope: sand, fill and paint bathroom with damp paint; paint all walls and ceiling in main room; replace bathroom lino; repair plug and shelf; replace bathroom tap.

Points to note:
- Bedroom carpet: we asked for a quote to replace the burnt carpet. The contractor advises it can stay. The check-out report records the burn as already present at check-in, so it can't be charged to the outgoing tenant; replacement would be your cost if you still want it. The carpet stains need professional cleaning – please say if you want a quote for that or a carpet replacement quote.
- Bath tap: the contractor has quoted to replace it, but we asked for a repair. We've asked them to confirm whether a cheaper repair will do.
- Water from the shower area has damaged the bathroom boxing and flooring. We've asked the contractor to find and fix the cause before laying new lino.
- We've asked for an itemised breakdown. This will show which costs may be recoverable from the tenant's deposit (e.g. new wall staining, cleaning and damaged items) and which are landlord costs (e.g. wear and tear, pre-existing damage).

Attachments: check-out inspection report; Alder Compliance estimate.
If you would prefer to use your own contractor or get a second quote, please let us know.

Kind regards,
Northbridge Lettings

model_notes:
The case is on hold waiting for the landlord. I've asked them to approve the £1,370 quote from Alder Compliance, which is over our £250 limit. The case file also contains a £1,190 invoice dated 9 March 2026, which is in the future. It must not be paid yet.

**Where things stood:** After the tenant moved out, the agency manager asked Alder Compliance for a quote for check-out works (job NBL-008-3466). The case history stops at that request. Alder Compliance's quote of £1,370 (dated 3 April 2025) is in the file, but nothing shows the landlord has approved it or that an order was raised.

**Records:** Our database has nothing for this flat, its tenancy or its repair history. I used the case file as the record, so the landlord's details haven't been checked against our records.

**What I did:**
- **Ticket:** Opened ticket TKT-716BC8 as a routine job, since the flat is empty and there's no safety risk.
- **Landlord approval:** Requested approval for £1,370 (approval APR-E0118B).
- **Landlord email:** Sent the standard quote-approval email (delivered). It explains:
  - The contractor left the bedroom carpet out of the quote. The burn was already recorded at check-in, so it can't be charged to the outgoing tenant. Replacing it would be the landlord's cost.
  - Water from the shower area has damaged the bathroom boxing and flooring. We've asked the contractor to find and fix the cause first.
  - Some costs may come out of the tenant's deposit once the quote is broken down by item.
- **Contractor email:** Sent to Alder Compliance (delivered). It tells them not to start work or invoice until we place an order, and asks them to:
  - break the quote down by item and confirm whether it includes VAT;
  - say what "repair plug socket" means. The inspection report says the basin plug is broken. If it's an electrical socket, the work needs a registered electrician.
  - say whether the bath tap can be repaired rather than replaced, as we asked;
  - say what is causing the water from the shower and whether fixing it is in the quote;
  - say whether they can quote for professionally cleaning the carpet stains.
- **Internal note and status:** Logged the issues below in an internal note. Set the status to "awaiting landlord", with a chase date of 8 April 2025.

**Problems in the paperwork:**
- **Dates:** The inspection was dated 5 January 2026 and signed after the case opened. The invoice is dated 9 March 2026. Treat both dates as unreliable.
- **Invoice:** Nothing was approved or ordered, and there are no photos of finished work or any reference number. Its £1,190 is below the quote and leaves out the tap. That's fine only if it's confirmed when the work is checked as complete.
- **Duplicate report:** Attachments 01 and 03 are two versions of the same check-out report with the same findings.
- No document contained hidden instructions trying to redirect me.

**Next steps for a person:**
1. Chase the landlord on 8 April 2025 if there's no reply; if there's still no answer after that, escalate to a manager.
2. When the landlord approves and Alder Compliance has answered, raise the order and do the completion check: photos, invoice compared with the quote, and confirmation of the tap.
3. The property manager decides what to deduct from the deposit, using the itemised quote. Likely tenant costs: new wall stains, carpet and mattress stains, the missing table and chair, dumped items and cleaning. Likely landlord costs: the carpet burn that was there at check-in, the dripping tap, and whatever is causing the shower leak.
